releases.body:
Release candidate for Gaia 5.8.0, cut from `release/5.8.0`. It is published to npm under the `rc` dist-tag; `latest` stays on 5.7.1, and `main` -- what plugin users who pin nothing receive -- is not touched by this release.

## Installing it

An RC installs by the same route a stable will: the plugin is pinned to the tag `v5.8.0-rc.2` and npm installs the exact version `5.8.0-rc.2`. Never install a dist-tag (`@rc`, `@latest`): it names whatever the registry serves at that moment.

1. Read the machine as it is: `gaia doctor --channels --workspace <folder>`. It shows every channel present (the Claude Code plugin, npm in the workspace and globally, OpenCode, the `gaia` on PATH), with what is declared, installed and running, and the database schema each copy expects. Note its verdict before changing anything.
2. Read the steps to this version: `gaia doctor --target 5.8.0-rc.2 --workspace <folder>`. It lists each gap and the command or settings edit that closes it, in order, spelled the way this machine declares it, with the folder to run it from. It runs nothing.
3. Run those steps one at a time, reading each answer. For npm, wait until `npm view @jaguilar87/gaia@5.8.0-rc.2 version` prints the version (the registry answers `E404` for a few minutes after a publish), then install it with `--save-exact`. For the plugin, re-add the marketplace at `#v5.8.0-rc.2` with the source typed exactly as declared, then update each install at its own scope from its project folder. Never use `claude plugin marketplace remove` to update: it deletes the cache running sessions load from.
4. Read the machine again: `gaia doctor --channels` must exit 0, every channel at 5.8.0-rc.2 with provenance `match`. Exit 1 means leftovers; exit 2 means the install did not come out right.
5. Restart: a new session or `/reload-plugins` for the plugin; restart Claude Code or OpenCode for npm.

Going back is the same flow with `--target <previous version>`.

## Your data

`gaia migrate plan` (run with the new copy's `gaia`) shows the chain your database goes through, whether `gaia migrate apply` needs `--consent-chain`, and the backups on hand, newest first. Every migration runs in one transaction after a verified backup. To return to an older version past a migration, `gaia migrate restore --from <backup>` puts a backup back: it checks the backup first, keeps the database it replaces as a `pre-restore` backup, and copies under the database's lock so open sessions never see a half-swapped file. Never copy `gaia.db` by hand.

## Your first sessions after installing

Every session start now runs a sweep that removes what a dead run left behind: Gaia's per-dispatch temp folders, scratch entries and worktrees whose owning session has ended and that have been quiet for 24 hours. A worktree with uncommitted or unpushed work, and anything whose owner cannot be read, is kept and listed instead.

- **The first sweep on a machine only lists.** After an install or an upgrade it removes nothing; the next session start says, in one line, what it would remove and that the following sweep removes it.
- **`GAIA_SESSION_SWEEP` sets what the sweep does:** `on` (the default) removes, `list` only records what it would remove, `off` disables it. An unknown value behaves as `list`.
- **To see the list yourself:** `gaia cleanup --sweep --dry-run` prints each item the sweep would remove or keep, with its size and reason. The automatic sweep never measures sizes.

## Background commands

A command started in the background keeps writing its output after the turn that started it is gone, and one unbounded search filled a small temp volume and stopped every session on the machine. So:

- **A background command must bound its output.** It is refused unless every stream it prints goes to a file under Gaia's scratch or tmp (`<command> &> ~/.gaia/scratch/<contract_id>.log`), to `/dev/null`, or through `head`, `tail` without follow, or `sleep`.
